findings.title: PR #342 is merge-conflicted, so the new sweep job cannot run and never has
findings.summary: validation-report.md's CI section says 'CI has simply not re-run since - not a failure, but not evidence for the current tree either.' That frames the absence as passive latency. It is not. `gh pr view 342` reports mergeable=false, mergeable_state='dirty': the branch is 113 commits behind origin/main and conflicts in two files, one of which is `.github/workflows/ci.yml` itself. GitHub cannot construct the pull_request merge ref for a dirty PR, so no pull_request workflow dispatches. Measured: 4df049b1 was pushed at 21:35:46Z and is the PR head; polled check-runs for that SHA at 21:40, 21:41, 21:42, 21:43 -> total_count=0 every time, 8 minutes post-push, while an unrelated PR on the same repo got its runs within ~30s at 21:25. Consequence: the requirement-traceability-sweep job -- the central deliverable of this change -- has ZERO live executions. Its only green CI history (2026-08-02, 4 runs) predates the job's current form by 13+ commits. The report's CI paragraph is factually true sentence by sentence but omits the blocking cause and leaves the reader believing a re-run would produce evidence; it would not.
findings.recommendation: Merge or rebase origin/main into the branch and resolve the ci.yml conflict (main added `context-eval` and `semantic-enablement-gate` jobs at the same tail region where this branch adds `requirement-traceability-sweep`; the resolution is additive, keep all three). Also resolve docs/architecture-analysis/contracts-inventory.md. Then re-push and require a green requirement-traceability-sweep before sign-off. Note the resolution edits the job definition itself, so the local 7.0b evidence is evidence for an artifact that will change before merge.

findings.title: VAL_FIX did not propagate to walkthrough-handoff.md, which still hands an agent the canonical path
findings.summary: 4df049b1 rewrote the canonical `skills/cite-requirements/scripts/walkthrough.py` runtime path in SKILL.md:63 and walkthrough.py:22, but the same WALK= line survives verbatim at walkthrough-handoff.md:34: `WALK="uv run --project packages/gen-eval python skills/cite-requirements/scripts/walkthrough.py"`. Not a CI breaker -- dependency_direction.py is invoked with --skills-root . from skills/, so it never scans openspec/ -- which is precisely why the linter went green without this file being touched. It is a live instruction an agent is told to copy. Same shape as the seven consecutive PLAN_REVIEW findings recorded in phase_history: the fix lands in the artifact the finding named, the artifact owning the consequence goes stale.
findings.recommendation: Update walkthrough-handoff.md:34 to the <skill-base-dir> form. Line 26 of the same file also asserts 'PR #342 (14/14 CI green as of last check)', which is now false (0 checks, dirty); it is hedged but worth correcting alongside V1-F1.

findings.title: 'matching test-infra-skills's effective scope' is not what CI runs
findings.summary: The report ran the skills suite as `uv run pytest -v -m "not e2e and not integration"` and parenthesises it as '(matching test-infra-skills's effective scope)'. CI line 69 runs `uv run pytest -v` with no marker filter, and skills/pyproject.toml's addopts adds only --import-mode=importlib. Checked the delta: the only marker-carrying file under skills/ is tests/autopilot/test_phase_archetype_e2e.py (pytestmark = pytest.mark.integration), and running it bare gives 3 failed, 2 passed (jsonschema 'write_capable' is a required property). Inert in practice -- tests/autopilot is not among the 38 testpaths entries, so CI never collects it either way, and these failures sit inside the ~1161-hidden-tests / 23-real-failures bucket this change's own pyproject comment documents and defers to a separate issue. The 2392 count is reproducible and correct; only the justification for the filter is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Drop the '-m' filter for the skills suite or restate the parenthetical as 'CI runs pytest unfiltered; the filter is inert here because no testpaths entry carries e2e/integration markers'.

assessment.note: Every quantitative claim in validation-report.md reproduced exactly (2392, 1213/2/37, 34/34, exit 0, 18-cite-14, 3 unchecked, 1015, 756).
